title: An analytic Jacobian unit certificate implies affinoid regularity
statement:
Let $F$ be a field complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, and let $r,s\geq0$. Write $T=F\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle$ for the ring of series $\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^r}a_
u x^
u$ such that for every $\epsilon>0$ only finitely many coefficients have $|a_
u|\geq\epsilon$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication. Choose $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in T$, put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ and $B=T/I$, and write bars for images in $B$. For $E\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$ and $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ with $|E|=|U|$, put $I_E=(f_j:j\in E)$ and $D_{E,U}=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i\in U,j\in E}$, ordering both subsets increasingly; partial derivatives are termwise derivatives and determinant is [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Set $(I_E:I)=\{a\in T:aI\subseteq I_E\}$. The empty determinant is $1$ and $I_\varnothing=0$. Form the ideal $H=\sum_{E,U}\overline{(I_E:I)}\, ar D_{E,U}B$ of $B$, where $\overline{(I_E:I)}$ denotes the image ideal. If $H=B$, then $B$ is a regular Noetherian ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. This implication holds in every characteristic, without any prior regularity or reducedness hypothesis on $B$, and includes $B=0$, $r=0$, and $s=0$.

source.place: Temkin, Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.20--21, converse Jacobian criterion, specialized to the ground field; the version for arbitrary real-valued complete fields is the same analytic Jacobian criterion, without the discrete formal model. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affinoid-polynomial-closed-point-comparison] with $n=r$ and polynomial ideal $J=0$. Its ring $C$ is $T$, so $T$ is Noetherian. Then $B=T/I$ is Noetherian directly from [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]: for an ideal $L\subset B$, its inverse image $L'\subset T$ is generated by finitely many $g_i$, and their images generate $L$ (lift an element of $L$ and its expression in the $g_i$). If $B=0$, it has no prime ideals and is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Henceforth consider a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of a nonzero $B$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.20--21, converse direction; agent reconstruction of regularity using the polynomial/Tate completed-local-ring comparison and Stacks Tags 07NY, 00NQ, 0AFS. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak n\subset T$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak m$, so $T/\mathfrak n=B/\mathfrak m=:\kappa$ is a field and $I\subset\mathfrak n$. Since $H=B$, some pair $E,U$ and some $a\in(I_E:I)$ have $\bar a\bar D_{E,U}\notin\mathfrak m$: otherwise every generator of every summand of $H$ would belong to $\mathfrak m$, forcing $H\subset\mathfrak m$. Thus $a,D_{E,U}\notin\mathfrak n$. Put $R=T_{\mathfrak n}$ and $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak nR$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $R$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$. The element $a/1$ is invertible; $aI\subset I_E\subset I$ therefore gives $IR=I_ER=(f_j/1:j\in E)$. This uses no equality of colon ideals after base change.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.20--21, converse direction; agent reconstruction of regularity using the polynomial/Tate completed-local-ring comparison and Stacks Tags 07NY, 00NQ, 0AFS. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The ring $R$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and Step 1. Put $P=F[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and $\mathfrak p=P\cap\mathfrak n$. The same $J=0$ case of [lem-trf-affinoid-polynomial-closed-point-comparison] says that $\mathfrak p$ is maximal and that the induced map gives $\widehat{P_{\mathfrak p}}\simeq\widehat R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], $P_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local], its completion is regular local. Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-ring-isomorphism] to this displayed isomorphism, and then the reverse implication of [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] for the Noetherian local ring $R$. This proves that $R$ is regular local without any assumption on the residue extension $\kappa/F$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.20--21, converse direction; agent reconstruction of regularity using the polynomial/Tate completed-local-ring comparison and Stacks Tags 07NY, 00NQ, 0AFS. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Each termwise $\partial_i$ preserves $T$: its coefficients are integer multiples of coefficients of the original series, and $|n|\leq1$ for every integer $n$. Comparing each coefficient in the finite Cauchy sums proves the Leibniz rule. Extend it to $R$ by $\partial_i(g/u)=((\partial_i g)u-g\partial_i u)/u^2$. This is well defined: if $v(gu'-g'u)=0$ with $v,u,u'\notin\mathfrak n$, differentiation and inversion of $v,u,u'$ give equality of the displayed fractions. Direct expansion gives Leibniz on $R$. Reduction modulo $\mathfrak q$ gives maps $\delta_i:R\to\kappa$ with $\delta_i(hh')=\bar h\delta_i(h')+\bar h'\delta_i(h)$. In particular they vanish on $\mathfrak q^2$. For $h\in\mathfrak q$ and $c\in R$, $\delta_i(ch)=\bar c\delta_i(h)$. Thus $h\mapsto(\delta_i h)_i$ induces a $\kappa$-linear map $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak q^2\to\kappa^r$. The identification $R/\mathfrak q=\kappa$ sends the residue of $g/u$ to $\bar g/\bar u$, with inverse $\bar g\mapsto[g/1]$, using the fractions of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.20--21, converse direction; agent reconstruction of regularity using the polynomial/Tate completed-local-ring comparison and Stacks Tags 07NY, 00NQ, 0AFS. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Order $E$ increasingly, write $c=|E|$, and call its elements $e_1,\ldots,e_c$; put $h_j=f_{e_j}/1$. Suppose $\sum_j\lambda_j[h_j]=0$ in $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak q^2$ with $\lambda_j\in\kappa$. Applying the map of Step 4 and projecting to the rows $U$ gives $M\lambda=0$, where $M=(\partial_i f_{e_j}\bmod\mathfrak n)_{i\in U,j}$. The determinant formula of [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] commutes with reduction term by term, so $\det M=D_{E,U}\bmod\mathfrak n\ne0$. The identity [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] gives $(\det M)\lambda=0$. Since $\kappa$ is a field, $\lambda=0$. Hence $[h_1],\ldots,[h_c]$ are linearly independent in $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak q^2$. If $c=0$, this is the empty independent family; the empty minor is $1$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.20--21, converse direction; agent reconstruction of regularity using the polynomial/Tate completed-local-ring comparison and Stacks Tags 07NY, 00NQ, 0AFS. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $0\leq j\leq c$ set $R_j=R/(h_1,\ldots,h_j)$, whose maximal ideal is the image $\mathfrak q_j$ of $\mathfrak q$. Inductively $R_j$ is regular local. The base $j=0$ is Step 3. For $j<c$, the image of $h_{j+1}$ lies in $\mathfrak q_j$ and not in $\mathfrak q_j^2$: otherwise $h_{j+1}\in\mathfrak q^2+(h_1,\ldots,h_j)$, and reducing its coefficients modulo $\mathfrak q$ would put $[h_{j+1}]$ in the $\kappa$-span of $[h_1],\ldots,[h_j]$, contrary to Step 5. Here the inverse image of $\mathfrak q_j^2$ is exactly $\mathfrak q^2+(h_1,\ldots,h_j)$ by multiplying representatives. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion] applied to $R_j$ proves $R_{j+1}$ regular local. At $j=c$, Step 2 identifies $R_c=R/IR$, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] identifies this ring with $B_{\mathfrak m}$. By [lem-trf-regular-local-ring-isomorphism], $B_{\mathfrak m}$ is regular local. For $c=0$ no induction step is needed.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.20--21, converse direction; agent reconstruction of regularity using the polynomial/Tate completed-local-ring comparison and Stacks Tags 07NY, 00NQ, 0AFS. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Finally fix any prime $\mathfrak l\subset B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal], choose a maximal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak l$. The ideal $\mathfrak lB_{\mathfrak m}$ is prime: $b/u$ belongs to it exactly when $b\in\mathfrak l$, since $u\notin\mathfrak m$ implies $u\notin\mathfrak l$, and this criterion verifies properness and primeness. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] its localization in the regular local ring $B_{\mathfrak m}$ is regular local. This ring is $B_{\mathfrak l}$: [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization](2) makes $B_{\mathfrak l}$ a localization of $B_{\mathfrak m}$ at the images of $B\setminus\mathfrak l$, and these are precisely the numerators of fractions outside $\mathfrak lB_{\mathfrak m}$, whose denominators are already units. The resulting isomorphism sends $(b/u)/(v/w)$ to $bw/(uv)$. Regularity transfers by [lem-trf-regular-local-ring-isomorphism]. Step 1 and [def-weil-regular-scheme] now give the conclusion. If $r=0$ or $s=0$ the same argument uses the empty families; no reducedness, perfectness, discreteness, or characteristic-zero assumption was used.
